statement: If any number of magnitudes be proportional, as one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents, so will all the antecedents be to all the consequents.
heath_proof: Let any number of magnitudes A, B, C, D, E, F be proportional, so that, as A is to B, so is C to D and E to F; I say that, as A is to B, so are A, C, E to B, D, F. For of A, C, E let equimultiples G, H, K be taken, and of B, D, F other, chance, equimultiples L, M, N. Then since, as A is to B, so is C to D, and E to F, and of A, C, E equimultiples G, H, K have been taken, and of B, D, F other, chance, equimultiples L, M, N, therefore, if G is in excess of L, H is also in excess of M, and K of N, if equal, equal, and if less, less; so that, in addition, if G is in excess of L, then G, H, K are in excess of L, M, N, if equal, equal, and if less, less. Now G and G, H, K are equimultiples of A and A, C, E, since, if any number of magnitudes whatever are respectively equimultiples of any magnitudes equal in multitude, whatever multiple one of the magnitudes is of one, that multiple also will all be of all. [V. 1] For the same reason L and L, M, N are also equimultiples of B and B, D, F; therefore, as A is to B, so are A, C, E to B, D, F. [V. Def. 5]

5.12
**Statement:** If any number of magnitudes be proportional, as one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents, so will all the antecedents be to all the consequents.

**Step 1.** Let any number of magnitudes A, B, C, D, E, F be proportional, so that, as A is to B, so is C to D and E to F; that is, A, B, C, D, E, F have the same ratio taken two and two (D5.6). Let A, C, E be the antecedents and B, D, F the consequents. I say that, as A is to B, so are A, C, E together to B, D, F together.

**Step 2.** Of A, C, E take any equimultiples whatever G, H, K, so that G, H, K are the same multiple of A, C, E respectively; and of B, D, F take any other equimultiples whatever L, M, N, so that L, M, N are the same multiple of B, D, F respectively.

**Step 3.** Since A is to B as C is to D, and G, H have been taken as equimultiples of A, C, while L, M are equimultiples of B, D, it follows from the definition of magnitudes in the same ratio (D5.5) that, if G exceeds L, H also exceeds M; if G is equal to L, H is equal to M; and if G is less than L, H is less than M.

**Step 4.** In the same way, since A is to B as E is to F, and G, K are equimultiples of A, E, while L, N are equimultiples of B, F, by D5.5, if G exceeds L, K also exceeds N; if equal, equal; and if less, less.

**Step 5.** Therefore, if G exceeds L, then H exceeds M and K exceeds N, so that the sum G, H, K together exceeds the sum L, M, N together. If G is equal to L, then H is equal to M and K is equal to N, so that G, H, K together are equal to L, M, N together, since equals added to equals give equal wholes (CN2). And if G is less than L, then H is less than M and K is less than N, so that G, H, K together fall short of L, M, N together.

**Step 6.** Now G, H, K are the same multiple of A, C, E respectively; therefore G, H, K together is the same multiple of A, C, E together that G is of A (5.1). Similarly, L, M, N are the same multiple of B, D, F respectively; therefore L, M, N together is the same multiple of B, D, F together that L is of B (5.1).

**Step 7.** Thus G and the sum G, H, K are equimultiples of the first A and the third A, C, E together, while L and the sum L, M, N are equimultiples of the second B and the fourth B, D, F together; and G, H, K were any equimultiples whatever, as were L, M, N. By Step 5, the multiple G of A and the multiple G, H, K of A, C, E together alike exceed, are alike equal to, or alike fall short of the multiple L of B and the multiple L, M, N of B, D, F together respectively.

**Step 8.** Therefore, by the definition of the same ratio (D5.5), as A is to B, so are A, C, E together to B, D, F together. That is, as one of the antecedents is to one of the consequents, so are all the antecedents to all the consequents. Q.E.D.
